newsitem.title: HUNGARY: TVK, MOL in steep rise on mkt.
newsitem.headline: TVK, MOL in steep rise on mkt.

text.p: Shares in Hungarian chemicals company TVK gained more than three percent on Monday on investor belief that the paper will maintain its level when it begins to trade without dividend coupons on Tuesday.
"If the trend remains (rising), TVK's price might remain, and then investors can put the 80 forint dividend into their pockets," one trader said.
At 1052 GMT TVK shares traded at 2,870 forints, up 100 forints or 3.61 percent.
TVK's shareholders approved at the company's recent annual general meeting the payout of an eight percent dividend on the 1996 earnings.
Oil company MOL rose despite a newspaper report which said that Hungarian privatisation agency APV Rt would not sale a further stake before October 15, the trader said.
At 1052 GMT it traded at 3,570 forints, up 125 forints or 3.63 percent.

The trader added that further factor in MOL's price rise was its weak supply which meant that the buyer had to push the price higher if wanted to acquire bigger amounts of shares, while the news that MOL found oil in Hungary attributed less.

MOL announced on Monday that it had discovered oil reserves in Savoly-South, an area in production since 1980, with the reserves may be significantly higher than the previously expected 2.5 million barrels.
